newsitem.title: GERMANY: Support for Kohl government is on the slide-poll.
newsitem.headline: Support for Kohl government is on the slide-poll.

text.p: Support among Germans for Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government is waning further, according to a poll carried out for the German public television station ZDF published on Friday.

The Politbarometer poll conducted by the Electoral Research group reported that 62 percent of Germans interviewed in May thought Kohl's government was doing a bad job, the highest level of dissatisfaction for four years.

Kohl's personal popularity also slid, with 42 percent of those polled supporting him, compared with 45 percent in April. Oskar Lafontaine, leader of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), saw his support grow to 41 percent from 39.

The strongest support was again seen for Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder, widely seen as a potential SPD candidate for the chancellor's job in the elections next year. Fifty-six percent of Germans preferred him to Kohl as chancellor.

The random telephone poll of 1,232 Germans showed that if an election was called now, the SPD would capture 38 percent of the votes and the Green Party 10 percent, which would give a so-called "red-green" coalition a parliamentary majority.

Support for the ruling Christian Democrats (CDU) and their Bavarian sister party the CSU dropped one point to 38 percent, with support for the Free Democrat (FDP) junior coalition party unchanged from April at five percent.
The poll sponsors said the poll had a margin of error of 2.5 percent for the larger parties and 1.5 percent for the smaller ones.
